comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup disclose activities related to the sale of loans during 2024. Goldman Sachs reports providing seller financing in connection with the sale of $4.44 billion of loans, primarily related to GreenSky. Citigroup discloses that it sold or reclassified $5.2 billion of corporate loans during 2024. While the specific loan types (consumer/originated vs. corporate) differ, both disclose significant loan sales activity in the same fiscal year under Item 8.

sentences.text: Additionally, the firm provided seller financing of $2.12 billion in connection with the sale of $4.44 billion of loans (the vast majority of which were related to GreenSky) during 2024 and of approximately $2.7 billion in connection with the sale of $3.24 billion of Marcus loans during 2023.
The Company sold and/or reclassified to held-for-sale $5.2 billion and $5.7 billion of corporate loans during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

The provided candidates for MS discuss netting of secured financing liabilities and representations/warranties on whole loan sales. While MS discloses representations and warranties on whole loan sales (c_2024_8_D309), the target disclosure specifically focuses on the mechanics and volume of seller financing provided *in connection with* loan sales (financing the buyer/transaction), whereas MS focuses on the post-sale liabilities arising from breaches of representations and warranties. The topics are related but distinct in nature (financing provision vs. warranty liability). Furthermore, MS does not disclose the volume of loan sales or financing provided in the same manner as GS. Given the specificity of 'Seller Financing Activities' in the target, and the lack of volume/financing details in MS candidates, they are not sufficiently comparable.
